name: Ode, the Tax-Collector
summary: The market's tax-collector. He comes for the smell of money, and gently squeezes out-of-town merchants who flash wealth. He fears his superiors and the inquisitor; he fears nothing in a lone woman merchant — unless there seems to be something unaccountable behind her.

knows: Who sold well today and how much to skim
Which bribe will buy his silence
The inquisitor has put a bounty on the town

reactions.bribe: Take the coins and look away (coins-, no suspicion rise)
reactions.flaunt_wealth: Saffron and the like shown in the open → he latches on for a heavy levy
reactions.intimidated: Cowed by a note or a cold air → he sulks off, but bears a grudge
